summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: @servicetitan/suppress-warnings@38.1.1 declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers _0xXXXX, per-function string-lookup proxy objects) and, on npm install, downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<arch>.zip, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB obfuscated Bun-CJS bundle (header '// @bun @bun-cjs', string-array shuffle routine, hex-named identifiers, indexed string-array destinations rather than plain URL literals) whose contents are unrelated to the package's advertised purpose (React warning suppression, dist/index.js is 126 bytes). The Bun runtime is used specifically to execute install-time code outside the reach of Node-based analysis tooling. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern combined with lifecycle-script obfuscation and a large opaque bundled payload matches the install-time-rce attack shape; the payload's behavior is not visible without executing it, and installing this version runs it automatically.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
